open_points.subject: A19-1 required proof
open_points.text: Witness, A19-1, A19-2: the test evidence of `_render_owner_page`, which renders every page of the owner interface [witness: note:_render_owner_page].
open_points.question: Must the A19-1 evidence show context-appropriate escaping for every stored field that can appear on every owner-interface page, or is exercising the page renderer with only the examples in Required tests 1 and 2 sufficient?
options: Show every renderable stored field in every applicable output context is escaped as text.
Show only the room-name and access-request examples.
Treat one test of the common renderer as proof without specifying which values and contexts it exercises.
open_points.default_guess: Require the test description to show every renderable stored field and each applicable rendering context, because A19-1 is universal.

witness.initial: A stored field other than a room name or access-request text appears on an owner page.
events: The owner stores markup in that field.
The owner opens the page that renders it.
outcomes: The field is escaped as text because the invariant and its evidence cover every renderable stored field.
Only the two named examples are guaranteed; this field's rendering is left to the implementation.

open_points.subject: A19-2 required proof
open_points.text: Witness, A19-2: for a value with a quote and a semicolon that is stored and read back as it was given, never as part of a command, the test evidence of `create_project` [witness: note:create_project].
open_points.question: What must the Required tests show to establish the universal A19-2 invariant across every stored-value path, including queries, commands, templates and imported data, rather than only `create_project` with one punctuation-bearing value?
options: Exercise or otherwise assert every boundary at which a stored or imported value could become interpreted structure.
Limit the guarantee to the `create_project` command path and browser renderer.
Name a complete shared boundary guarantee and require its check to cover all consumers.
open_points.default_guess: Require evidence covering every value-to-interpreter boundary, including import parsing and all query, command and template consumers.

witness.initial: An import field or a stored value used by an operation other than `create_project` contains syntax meaningful to its consumer.
events: The owner imports or stores the value.
Registry later processes the value through that consumer.
outcomes: The value remains data because A19-2 and its required evidence cover that boundary.
The untested consumer may interpret it because the named evidence covers only rendering and `create_project`.
witness.observer: the owner or store affected by the interpreted input

open_points.subject: A21 review after the A13 cookie change
open_points.text: Reviewed under injection_interpreted_input, browser_boundary and files_artifacts (A19) and browser_boundary (A13): no outcome changed.
open_points.question: Did the A13 cookie-attribute change also reopen `authentication_credential_abuse`, which names A13 and expressly covers session and token lifecycle, and if so what is that category's reviewed outcome?
options: Review `authentication_credential_abuse` and record whether its outcome changes.
Declare that the cookie-attribute change affects only `browser_boundary` and state why.
Treat naming `browser_boundary` alone as a complete rerun for A13.
open_points.default_guess: Reopen and record `authentication_credential_abuse`; retain APPLICABLE only after confirming its outcome.

witness.initial: A13 is referenced by both `browser_boundary` and `authentication_credential_abuse`.
events: The session cookie's attributes are changed to come from a provider constant.
A21 records a rerun only under `browser_boundary` for A13.
outcomes: The authentication category is reopened and reviewed because its session-lifecycle basis changed.
The authentication category remains closed without review because the change is classified solely as browser-boundary work.

open_points.subject: OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES secure-cookie guarantee
open_points.text: the session cookie's attributes are now one constant of the data provider, `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES`, with the same attributes as before.
open_points.question: Does “the same attributes as before” require the cookie to be HTTPS-only in every environment, as the earlier A21 review says, or only when the interface is reached from another machine, as A13 rule 1 requires?
options: The cookie is always HTTPS-only, including loopback use.
The cookie is HTTPS-only only when the interface is reached from another machine.
Local HTTP is unsupported, so the two formulations have the same observable outcome.
open_points.default_guess: Require it to be always HTTPS-only because A21 previously calls that the existing stricter guarantee.

witness.initial: The owner reaches Registry locally over loopback HTTP, which the supplied rules do not prohibit.
events: The browser decides whether to return the session cookie on the next local HTTP request.
outcomes: An always-Secure cookie is not returned over local HTTP, so the session cannot be used there.
A conditionally Secure cookie is returned locally, while remote use remains HTTPS-only.
witness.observer: the owner using the local interface

open_points.subject: OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES representation
open_points.text: the session cookie's attributes are now one constant of the data provider, `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES`, with the same attributes as before.
open_points.question: What concrete type and framework-facing representation does the single constant use?
options: An immutable structured value with named cookie attributes.
A backend-specific mapping consumed by the HTTP adapter.
A validated provider value lowered into framework arguments during generation.
open_points.default_guess: Use an immutable structured value and lower it at the HTTP boundary.
consequences: A structured value makes the attributes explicit and type-checkable but requires an adapter to the chosen HTTP framework.
A backend-specific mapping is simpler at the call site but couples the provider constant to the framework.
A generated lowering keeps the design value backend-neutral but adds generated conversion code.
open_points.requirement: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.

open_points.subject: A21 cookie-constant passage
open_points.text: the session cookie's attributes are now one constant of the data provider, `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES`, with the same attributes as before.
open_points.rule: Таблица выше — исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`, настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: The passage must name it as `the imported OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES constant` while retaining the required cookie guarantees.
